summary: The note explains how seasonal fishing calendars support sustainable fishing and shape regional seafood dishes and festivals around the world. It surveys peak seasons and celebrations in the Northeastern U.S., Mediterranean Europe, the Pacific Northwest, Louisiana, Ireland, and Hokkaido. It also covers clams and scallops, technology's role in forecasting seasons, wine pairings, and the effects of climate change on seafood seasons.
one_line: Overview of seasonal fishing calendars, sustainable harvests, and the regional seafood dishes, festivals, and wine pairings tied to peak seasons worldwide.
key_facts: Josiah Simmons of Cape Cod follows strict fishing calendars and casts nets for Atlantic cod when they are abundant, typically in the early spring months.
Japanese fisherman Hiroshi Takahashi said, "We must fish responsibly to ensure our children can also enjoy the bounties of the sea."
Oyster season in New England starts around September, and Wellfleet, Massachusetts hosts oyster festivals; Wellfleet oysters are known for a sweet and briny flavor from cold waters.
Sicilian chef Isabella Rossi says late summer brings the Mediterranean red prawn, used in 'risotto al gambero rosso' and celebrated in town festivals in September and October.

Salmon season in the Pacific Northwest (Washington and Oregon) is in full swing by mid-September, and the Makah and Chinook tribes hold salmon festivals with dances, music, and communal fish preparation.

The Louisiana Shrimp and Petroleum Festival is held in late August in Morgan City, Louisiana, celebrating the relationship between the fishing and oil industries and serving shrimp gumbo, étouffée, and jambalaya.

The Galway International Oyster and Seafood Festival is held in the last week of September and is described as Ireland's oldest oyster festival, with eating contests, cooking demonstrations, and live music.
The Hokkaido Seafood Festival takes place in early October at the apex of the salmon and crab seasons, featuring 'kani miso' (crab innards) and 'ika' (squid).
Scallop bisque is enjoyed at Christmas dinners along the Brittany coast of France, while New England clam chowders are served in early September.
Michael Thompson of the Florida Keys uses marine technology and tradition to forecast fishing times; stone crab is most abundant from October to May.
Sommelier Chloe Dupont of Bordeaux says full-bodied white wines complement the Dungeness crab season in November.
In New Zealand, vintners prepare crisp Sauvignon Blancs for the green-lipped mussel season in March.
Marine Biologist Dr. Emily Sanchez monitors climate-driven changes to fishing calendars and works with local fisheries to adapt.
